issues.description: DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE is now defined in three places, complecting one fact across three modules.
issues.detail: The string 'python:3.12' is the canonical default, yet it lives in pipeline.py, the TS fallback in Commands.ts, and again as an exported const in CellMetadataEditor.tsx. That is one value, three identities, no single source of truth. When the default moves to 3.13, two of three will drift silently. Decompose: one constant on the backend, one fetched value on the frontend, no literal fallbacks elsewhere.

issues.description: Silent semantic change: empty base_image fallback now writes a concrete image, complecting 'unset' with 'default'.
issues.detail: Previously self.base_image = '' meant 'unset, let kfp decide'; now it means 'python:3.12'. These are different facts about the world — the absence of a value and a specific chosen value — and the diff collapses them. Downstream code (and the template's `or` chain) can no longer distinguish 'user said nothing' from 'system picked the default'. Keep the empty sentinel and resolve the default at render time only.

issues.description: Resolution of the effective base image is duplicated across template, dialog placeholder, and inline text.
issues.detail: The precedence rule step.config.base_image -> pipeline base_image -> default is reimplemented in nb_function_template.jinja2, the Dialog placeholder, and createBaseImageText. Three sites, one rule — classic complecting of policy with presentation. Extract one pure function resolveBaseImage(stepImage, pipelineImage, defaultImage) and call it from each site. The rule then has one home and one test.

issues.description: Replacing an inline Input with a modal dialog is easy-not-simple — more UI, same data.
issues.detail: The previous Input was one widget bound to one field. The new Button-opens-Dialog adds modal state (baseImageDialogOpen), a new toggle method, MUI Dialog imports, and a 'Reset to Default' button that just writes ''. The underlying value is still one string. This is familiar Material-UI patterning, not a simpler design. If the intent is 'show the default', a placeholder or helper text on the original Input carries that fact without the dialog machinery.

issues.description: Function-scope import of DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE inside get_default_base_image hides the dependency.
issues.detail: The `from kale.pipeline import DEFAULT_BASE_IMAGE` inside the function body adds nothing — there is no cycle to break here. Module-level import makes the data dependency visible and removes a per-call import lookup. Small thing, but it is the kind of incidental complication that compounds.

issues.description: RPC endpoint returns a constant, treating a static value as a service call.
issues.detail: get_default_base_image is a round-trip to fetch a string that never changes during a session. The frontend could receive it once at panel init alongside other config, or the backend could embed it in an existing bootstrap payload. As written, it is place-oriented code masquerading as a query. Not urgent, but worth noting before more 'get the constant' RPCs accrete.

review.summary: The change conflates one fact — the default base image — across three identities (Python constant, TS fallback, TS exported constant) and reimplements the resolution rule in three places. The pipeline.py change silently turns 'unset' into 'python:3.12', collapsing two distinct facts about the world into one. The dialog rewrite is familiar Material-UI work but not simpler than the Input it replaces; the underlying value is still a single string. Decision: COMPLECTED with EASY-NOT-SIMPLE on the UI rewrite. The question that should have been asked first: where does this value live, and who is allowed to know it.
